one_liner: SIMD-vectorized non-cryptographic hash family; XXH3 beats CityHash ~2.7x on in-RAM buffer bandwidth.
what_it_does: Non-cryptographic hash library with three families - XXH32, XXH64, and XXH3 (64/128-bit, vectorized) - for hashing in-RAM buffers, hash tables, checksums, and content-dedup keys. API is single-call one-shot functions (e.g. XXH3_64bits()) plus a streaming interface for unbounded/chunked input. Not a literal drop-in for CityHash's function names, but the same one-shot/streaming call shape.
how_it_is_fast: XXH3 uses vectorized arithmetic (SSE2/AVX2/AVX512/NEON/VSX/RVV/LoongArch LSX-LASX, auto-selected at compile time or runtime-dispatched) with multiply-and-fold mixing tuned for both large-buffer bandwidth and small-key latency. XXH_INLINE_ALL header-only mode lets the compiler inline and constant-fold hashing when key length is a compile-time constant, reported at roughly +200% for small keys. Optional runtime ISA dispatch (Makefile DISPATCH=1 / LIBXXH_DISPATCH=1) picks the best available vector unit at startup instead of requiring a fixed -m flag at build time.
when_to_use: Non-cryptographic hashing of in-RAM buffers where throughput dominates (checksums, hash tables, dedup, content-addressing)
Hot loops hashing small/fixed-length keys, using XXH_INLINE_ALL for compile-time-constant lengths
Need identical hash output across little/big-endian and 32/64-bit platforms
Embedded or constrained targets: XXH32 for 32-bit-only hardware, or XXH_NO_STDLIB to avoid malloc/free
Want SIMD speedup across x86 (AVX2/AVX512), ARM (NEON), POWER (VSX), or RISC-V (RVV) without hand-writing per-ISA paths
when_not_to_use: Cryptographic use cases (signatures, password storage, adversarial-input integrity) - README explicitly says do not use xxHash for these
Comparing against 32-bit-only hashes and expecting a width-matched number: the project's own Murmur3 benchmark row is the 32-bit variant, not matched to XXH3's 64/128-bit output
Raw single-thread bandwidth is the only criterion and the ~1.09x edge of wyhash (per catalog sibling entry) matters more than xxHash's broader platform/test-suite maturity
Distributing the xxhsum CLI where GPL-2.0-or-later is unacceptable (the library itself, xxhash.c/xxhash.h, is BSD-2-Clause and unaffected)
Need statically-allocated streaming state guaranteed correct with zero further testing: the streaming API has had real bugs in the past (see gotchas), now fixed but worth pinning a recent release

integration.form: source-drop (xxhash.c + xxhash.h); also buildable as static/shared libxxhash, or header-only via XXH_INLINE_ALL
integration.dependencies: none required; optional use of stdlib.h (malloc/free, disable via XXH_NO_STDLIB) and string.h (memcpy/memset/memcmp, redirectable via XXH_memcpy/XXH_memset/XXH_memcmp macros)
integration.min_toolchain: C90 (ANSI C) baseline with optional C99/C++11 feature detection; compiles cleanly as C++ via an extern "C" guard (disable with XXH_NO_EXTERNC_GUARD)
integration.platforms: x86/x64 (scalar, SSE2, AVX2, AVX512, runtime-dispatchable), aarch64/ARM (NEON), PowerPC (VSX), RISC-V (RVV), LoongArch (LSX/LASX), plus a portable scalar fallback everywhere; produces identical hashes on little- and big-endian systems
integration.thread_safety: not documented explicitly. One-shot calls (XXH32/XXH64/XXH3_64bits, etc.) are stateless and reentrant. XXH32_state_t/XXH64_state_t/XXH3_state_t streaming objects are not described as synchronized - do not share one state object across threads without external locking
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same one-shot/streaming call shape as CityHash but different function names (XXH3_64bits/XXH3_128bits vs CityHash64/CityHash128); call sites need updating

gotchas: Explicitly not a cryptographic hash - README warns against signatures, password storage, or adversarial-integrity use
Peak AVX2/AVX512 throughput needs either the matching -m compiler flag or Makefile DISPATCH=1/LIBXXH_DISPATCH=1 runtime dispatch; a naive build can silently run at scalar/SSE2 speed

Streaming API has a history of real bugs: issue #816 "Streaming hashing is broken" (2023) and #378 "Uneven chunk size in xxh3 stream computes wrong hash" (2020), both closed/fixed but signal the incremental path is the more fragile part of the API

XXH_FORCE_ALIGN_CHECK / XXH_FORCE_MEMORY_ACCESS build macros exist because some architectures need a different memory-access strategy for best performance; the defaults are auto-selected per architecture and may need tuning on unusual targets
pick_this_over_siblings_when: wyhash edges out XXH3 by roughly 1.09x bandwidth per the catalog sibling entry, but xxHash documents wider SIMD/architecture coverage (SSE2/AVX2/AVX512/NEON/VSX/RVV/LoongArch), a dedicated massive collision tester plus SMHasher pass, and a mature package ecosystem (vcpkg, Repology-tracked distro packages); pick xxHash when portability across architectures and test-suite maturity outweigh a single-digit-percent throughput gap.
verified_claims_summary: Project's own tests/bench program (Clang v10.0, -O3, Intel i7-9700K, Ubuntu 20.04 x64) measured XXH3 (AVX2) at 59.4 GB/s versus CityHash64 at 22.0 GB/s (~2.7x) and CityHash128 at 21.7 GB/s (~2.7x); versus Murmur3 (32-bit) at 3.9 GB/s (~15.2x, not width-matched). Small-data velocity: XXH3 133.1 vs City64 76.6 vs Murmur3 56.1.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-20, 11.3k stars, CHANGELOG shows ongoing RISC-V/LoongArch perf work); library (xxhash.c/xxhash.h) is BSD-2-Clause and trivially vendorable, while the separate xxhsum CLI is GPL-2.0-or-later.
